messages:
maria: heads up — master CI turned red after the poetry lock regen in PR #2345. Docker image build fails on pip install with a cryptography wheel error. anyone free to triage?

sam: i see the failure in the pipeline. opening job log now, can you paste the pip output you saw?

maria: pasted from job:```
Step 7/14 : RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
#11 4.512 Collecting cryptography
#11 4.513   Using cached cryptography-42.0.tar.gz (1.5 MB)
#11 4.513 ERROR: Could not build wheels for cryptography which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
#11 4.513 ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 1: /usr/local/bin/python -u -c 'import sys, setuptools, tokenize; sys.argv[0] = '"'"'/tmp/pip-install-xxxxx/setup.py'"'"'; __file__=sys.argv[0];...
The command '/bin/sh -c pip install -r requirements.txt' returned a non-zero code: 1
```

aj: that stack looks like pip tried to compile cryptography instead of using a wheel. likely the manylinux wheel tag changed or pip didn't find a compatible wheel. could be a transitive pin bumped a package that changed the wheel metadata.

frank: quick repro on local: `docker build` with `python:3.10-slim` + current requirements reproduces it. upgrading pip in the Dockerfile to latest (pip install -U pip setuptools wheel) makes the wheel install succeed. so temporary fix is to upgrade pip in image.

maria: ok workaround noted. i'd still like to bisect the lock regen because we have to be careful about changing the base image. can infra run a lockfile bisect between commits `20a1f2e..f9c3b7a`? i suspect a transitive bump (maybe cffi or wheel metadata).

olivia: pinging infra. @ci-bot can you queue a bisect runner? if we need manual help i can run on the dedicated mac runner. also, can someone run `poetry export -f requirements.txt --dev --without-hashes > reqs.txt` and diff the cryptography/cffi entries across the two lock versions?

ci-bot: queued: job `eng/ci/bisect-lockfile` (run 867). https://ci.internal/runs/867 — status: queued

sam: i ran `poetry export` locally. lock regen moved `cffi` 1.17.4 -> 1.17.6 and pulled `pyOpenSSL` 23.x in as a top-level transient. that could change wheel tags for cryptography. trying to reproduce by pinning cffi back.

maria: thanks. if pinning cffi makes the Docker build succeed then we know transitive is the culprit. frank — can you try a quick rebuild with `cffi==1.17.4` pinned in the exported requirements?

frank: done. rebuild succeeded locally with pinned cffi. looks like that bumped the build path for cryptography. i'll hold off on any global changes until we confirm. :thumbsup:

olivia: i'll standby to run the CI bisect results once the worker finishes. if bisect confirms the cffi bump, propose we revert that transitive change in the lockfile and open a follow-up PR that upgrades pip in the Docker image as a second change so we don't hit this again.

maria: plan sounds good. small action items: (1) frank to open a quick revert PR for the lockfile if bisect confirms, (2) sam to add pip upgrade step to Dockerfile in a follow-up PR, (3) olivia to run CI bisect and paste findings here. i'll watch for PRs and merge once green.

sam: one more note — if we revert the lockfile we should include a short note in the commit message explaining the wheel/platform compatibility issue so future lock regens pay attention.

ci-bot: build rerun triggered for `eng/ci/image-build` (id 543) — https://ci.internal/jobs/543 — status: running

maria: thanks everyone. i'll be AFK for 90m but will check back. if someone gets a green PR, ping me.@here

(15m later)
sam: quick update: bisect run finished — culprit identified: transitive bump of `cffi` from 1.17.4 -> 1.17.6 pulled in a wheel build path incompatibility with our slim base. bisect log: https://ci.internal/runs/867/logs. frank please proceed with revert PR.

frank: opening PR now — #2352 revert lockfile transitive bump, includes note about wheel tags and link to this thread. cc: @maria @sam

maria: perfect. once CI on the revert is green i'll merge and then we can follow up with the pip-upgrade Dockerfile PR. thanks all for the quick triage! :partyparrot:
